LESSON: WRITING 2.4.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Writing 2.4.1 Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.4.1 Handwriting, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What should we do to ensure we write legibly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  Look at sample of a text with good handwriting.  Identify aspects of good handwriting such as letter formation, spacing, alignment, capitalisation. Learners with speech difficulties can identify orally, by typing or writing.  Copy letter patterns of the target letter-sound combinations (dr’, ‘fl’, ‘fr’ and ‘gl’), with peers. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  Look at sample of a text with good handwriting.  Identify aspects of good handwriting such as letter formation, spacing, alignment, capitalisation. Learners with speech difficulties can identify orally, by typing or writing.  Copy letter patterns of the target letter-sound combinations (dr’, ‘fl’, ‘fr’ and ‘gl’), with peers. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.4.1 Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication: The learner’s ability to write clearly and correctly is enhanced as they write words related to the theme in

good handwriting.

 Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to learn independently is improved as they practise writing neatly and legibly on their

own.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates the effort of and assists peers who are struggling with handwriting.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Learner Support Programmes (Peer Education and Mentorship): The learner’s ability to mentor others is enhanced as they

demonstrate aspects of good handwriting to peers.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to apply the handwriting skills learnt in learning of similar concept in Kiswahili Language Activities.
